data.name: Elminage ORIGINAL - Priestess of Darkness and The Ring of the Gods
data.detailed_description:
FACELOAD＆SOUNDLOAD

FACELOAD is a function where a player can choose an image they like and use it as a character's icon. Instructions 1) Place your chosen image in the folder 'My Document' > 'Mebius' > 'Elminage Original' > 'FACELOAD' The FACELOAD folder will automatically be created upon upgrade. Supported image file and size 192x192px JPG, BMP, PMG file 2 ) Start the game and select 'FACELOAD' 3 ) Choose a location to upload the image 4 ) The image in the FACELOAD folder will be shown. Select the image to upload. 5 ) The image should be ready. Press 'Z' to finish the process. Begin the game and when you go to the face list in 'adventurer registration' or 'change name' at the Training School, select FACELOAD on the bottom right icon where you can find your face.


SOUNDLOAD

SOUNDLOAD is a function where a player can use a BGM they like in the game. Instructions 1 ) Place your chosen image in the folder 'My Document' > 'Mebius' > 'Elminage Original' > 'SOUNDLOAD' Supported sound files wav. or ogg. 2 ) Start the game and select 'SOUNDLOAD' 3 ) Go to the sound page 4 ) The sound file in the SOUNDLOAD folder will be shown. Select the file to upload. Pressing PAGE DOWN adjusts the volume. Pressing 'F' returns the sound back to its original setting. 5 ) The image should be ready. Press 'Z' to finish the process. There may be parts of the image unable to be reproduced depending on the type/format of the file. Please seek approval beforehand. In the case SOUNDLOAD does not work normally, the steps below can return you to the original setting. 1 ) Confirm whether there is a BIN folder the 'Elminage Original¥SOUNLOAD folder'. 2 ) Rename, or if that fails, delete the SNLD.DAT in the BIN folder.


Acerca do jogo

ABOUT THE GAME For all budding adventurers, the king of 3D dungeon crawler RPGs - 'Elminage ORIGINAL - Priestess of Darkness and The Ring of the Gods ' - has finally arrived on Steam. The original 3D dungeon RPG has returned! Create and raise your characters to defeat the monsters that lurk deep in the labyrinth-like dungeons. Its simple gameplay and sense of freedom makes you feel like you are truly inside a fantasy world. Choose from 16 occupation including the likes of Fighter, Mage and Samurai. With 9 races to choose from, diverse parties can be created set according to gender, age and their personality. In addition, customize the game to your liking with the graphic/sound functions. With many events along the way, fulfill the main quest to search for the 5 rings. Let's open the gates and head out to a new adventure. About Configuration Settings Opening the Elminage Original Config.exe file in the installation folder accesses key config, game pad settings, window size. Alt+Enter changes between full screen/window Alt+F4 closes the game.

reviews.review:
I'm coming into Elminage Original after playing Elminage Gothic, since Gothic is the more famous of the two, and is arguably better, though not necessarily for the same audiences.

As far as Wizardry games go, I'd rate Elminage solidly in the middle. It's in no way a game that goes out and destroys you the moment you step into the first dungeon, but it's certainly not an easy game and there's plenty of monsters that will summarily put your entire party in a grave if you don't treat them seriously. It has all the usual Wizardry systems, such as the need for body recovery if you wipe in a dungeon and the risk of characters turning to ash and being lost if you get bad rolls on resurrections, but much of these are tampered back -- I resurrected tons of characters, and only had maybe three turn to ash, and none of them every get lost. There are items to deal with the worse of these systems, but unlike Gothic, the encounters are fair enough that I was willing to accept the losses and work with the ingame systems rather than savescum every doorway, so it makes the game accessible for those wanting to try out a challenging Wizardry-esque crawler even if it might not hit all the masochistic G-spots for those looking for the punishing experience. That's not to say there isn't a punishing part of the game if you want to start playing beheading roulette and getting bombed with Enterook Mista every third attack, but this is entirely connected to the postgame dungeon.

One of my major praises for Gothic was the incredible dungeon design. There are flourishes of this in Original, but this was by far and wide the biggest disappointment in the game. While the dungeons have their own aesthetic in the 3D dungeon view, and most of them have a gimmick involved with getting through them, the maps are almost all 20x20 blocks of square rooms going into more square rooms and corridors, which becomes somewhat repetitive in terms of exploring. Once you've done the first dungeon, every other one becomes available, and while they have a ramping difficulty shown by the number of skulls out of five they're given, the reality is that difficulty largely applies only to the very bottom/top of the place. In fact, there is very little variation in the monsters between, since most early floors bombard you with the same monsters in varying degrees of combinations. This gives you the freedom to explore where you want to, but again, takes some of the uniqueness of the places away to the point where it quickly feels like you're doing the same thing over and over.

Speaking of monsters ... there's a damn lot! I praised Gothic for it's huge cast of creatures, but now seeing Original, I realise almost all of wonderful designs were already done here. It was funny walloping down in a couple of blows creatures that I'd learned to dread, but I digress. There's a lot of monsters, and they rarely double up, meaning you're often getting into battles with 3-15 different creatures all throwing their own style of attacks at you. This does break up the monotony some, and if you're not familiar with the designs from Gothic, there's a lot of enjoyment to be found in finding them.

The classes are solidly designed and there's a lot of unique things to be done with some of the more creative additions like the summoner. The alchemy system is rather barebones compared to what it became in its successor, but it's good enough to add some spice for those getting a feel for the genre. There's also a large quest pool with 50-55 things to direct your exploring. These aren't the most amazing things, and if you're not finding item A in dungeon B, you're often having to experiment with unique class abilities that will likely require you to look it up in the online guides of which there are very few and are pretty hard to find in the first place, but there are ingame options to get additional information and clues to direct you along the way. The game also features a New Game+ option, whereby you can carry over your team and items and start from the beginning, either with new or to continue developing old favourites.

I'd say it probably took me ~40-45 hours to fully explore the main world and do most of the quests. I then spent 15 or so hours in the post game dungeon, of which I got to the end boss, though I never levelled high enough to stand a chance against him. My understanding is that there's a harder variation of the storyline end boss if you go through New Game+, but seeing as I still carry the scars from Gothic, I wasn't inclined to push through for that.

Regardless, it's a really solid dungeon crawler that's totally worth the money for those who want to dabble in what Wizardry type games are like, with traps on every chest and the thrill of identifying your items and figuring out whether they're an upgrade. If you're well accustomed to this style of game you'd probably be better off skipping to it's sequel, since you'd be getting everything this has to offer and more. But if your a more casual participant in the series, definitely give this one a go. It's hard enough to give you a sense of accomplishment for beating it, but not so bad that it'll turn you away by the end of the first dungeon.
